mutation_targets.rationale: F_PermissionGate is the load-bearing constraint that ties op.succeeded to the (role,kind) matrix plus ownership. Removing it lets a non-owner non-admin member succeed at DeleteTask; the injection forces such an op into the universe, which LeastPrivilege/OwnershipBasedAccess are supposed to catch.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_LeastPrivilege { some op: Operation, m: TeamMembership | some op.succeeded and m.user = op.caller and m.team = op.teamCtx and m.role = MemberRole and op.kind = DeleteTask and some op.target and op.target.owner != op.caller }

mutation_targets.rationale: F_CrossTeamIsolation is what forbids a successful operation from reaching a task whose team differs from the caller's X-Team-Id. Clearing it allows cross-tenant access; the injection forces a successful GetTaskById whose target lives in a different team than teamCtx — exactly the leak NoInformationLeakage should flag. GetTaskById is used (not PATCH/DELETE) so no audit-task team chain re-enforces isolation.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_CrossTeam { some op: Operation | some op.succeeded and op.kind = GetTaskById and some op.target and op.target.team != op.teamCtx }

mutation_targets.rationale: F_StateChangingOpsProduceAudit forces every successful POST/PATCH/DELETE to emit exactly one audit entry. Clearing it lets a mutation slip through unaudited; the injection forces a successful PostTasks with no producedAudit, which AuditCompleteness/FR-015 is supposed to catch.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditMissing { some op: Operation | some op.succeeded and op.kind = PostTasks and no op.producedAudit }

mutation_targets.rationale: F_AppendOnlyAuditEntries says every audit row must be tied to exactly one originating operation — there are no orphans, no double-attribution. Removing it allows audit entries to appear without a producing op (i.e., 'injected' rows). The injection forces such an orphan, which AppendOnly should catch.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnly { some ae: AuditEntry | no op: Operation | op.producedAudit = ae }

mutation_targets.rationale: F_AuditAttribution binds the audit entry's actor and team to the operation's caller and teamCtx. Clearing it permits an audit row whose actor differs from the operation's caller — a misattribution. The injection forces such a mismatch, which AttributionCorrectness/FR-002 is supposed to catch.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_Attribution { some op: Operation, ae: AuditEntry | ae = op.producedAudit and ae.actor != op.caller }

mutation_targets.rationale: F_TaskOwnerIsTeamMember anchors a task's owner to a real membership in the task's team. Removing it lets a task carry an owner who has no membership row. The injection forces such a task — exactly what OwnershipExclusivity/FR-006 is supposed to catch.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OwnerNotMember { some t: Task | no m: TeamMembership | m.user = t.owner and m.team = t.team }
